rationale: The long-term targets of a score around 500 are part of 'Our National Mission'. The performance of more able and talented children in level 6 and level 5 scores is below the OECD average.
conditions: More work needs to be done on reading, and lessons will be learned from southern Ireland's success with reading scores.

evidence.quote: Well, those long-term targets of a score around 500 are part of 'Our National Mission', and we have to keep the pressure on to strive. They are testing, but we have to keep the pressure on to strive to reach them. In some cases, I can be quite encouraged. If we look at reading scores for girls, we are almost there, but that just demonstrates what a journey we've got with our boys to address.
evidence.speaker: Kirsty Williams AM

evidence.quote: So, I think that's where we really need to push on. That's one of the reasons why we have introduced a more able and talented budget to support that, and our Seren programme, which is delivering fantastic results post-16. That's why we're introducing the principles of Seren earlier into children's careers, bringing it down from year 9 upwards, to be able to drive improvements.
evidence.speaker: Kirsty Williams AM

evidence.quote: Even within the UK, really, we are quite far behind.
evidence.speaker: Suzy Davies AM

evidence.quote: The balloon needs to be bigger not just squeezing it at one end.
evidence.speaker: Suzy Davies AM

evidence.quote: I just want to discuss an issue that I know is important to you, namely closing the attainment gap between pupils who are eligible for free school meals and those who are not eligible for free school meals. Unfortunately, the problem persists, doesn't it?
evidence.speaker: Sian Gwenllian AM

records.decision: The decision is to continue supporting learners who are eligible for free school meals, looked-after children, and some children from ethnic minority groups, and to focus resources on these children earlier, starting from nursery and formal education at age 5.
rationale: We are not where we need to be in terms of the performance of our children on free school meals, looked-after children, and some children from some ethnic minority groups. There has been some progress in some areas, but it is not where I would want it to be.
conditions: Progress has been made, but not where I would want it to be.

evidence.quote: We will continue to look to support those learners in a variety of ways, again looking to amend our practice on the basis of evidence that is given to us from our experts who are there to advise us.
evidence.speaker: Kirsty Williams AM

evidence.quote: But, I do think that we need to acknowledge where progress has been made.
evidence.speaker: Kirsty Williams AM

evidence.quote: If we look at pupils who are eligible for free school meals, they do score below their better-off counterparts in PISA by some 34 points. The gap in England is 40 points. So, again, that gap is smaller here in Wales.
evidence.speaker: Kirsty Williams AM

evidence.quote: That's why we will continue to focus those resources on those children, where we need it.
evidence.speaker: Kirsty Williams AM

records.decision: A ring-fenced grant of £10 million will be maintained to support education of minority ethnic children.
records.topic: education funding for minority ethnic children
rationale: To support education of minority ethnic children.
conditions: The need for a more sophisticated conversation about what is really going on in attainment across minority ethnic groups.

evidence.quote: Yes, and that's why we have committed to maintaining a ring-fenced grant to local authorities of some £10 million, to support education of our minority ethnic children.
evidence.speaker: Kirsty Williams AM

records.decision: The committee resolved to meet in private for the remainder of the meeting.
rationale: In accordance with Standing Order 17.42.

evidence.quote: Can I propose, in accordance with Standing Order 17.42, that the committee resolves to meet in private for the remainder of the meeting? Are Members content? Thank you.
evidence.speaker: Kirsty Williams AM
